text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1814042222 — Elevated 5xx and queue time in Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42. Error rate spiked ~3x starting ~14:03 UTC. P95 latency rising, autoscale at cap. Paging oncall.
michael: Acknowledged. Looking now — checking autoscale events + node utilization.
lina: I see autoscale hit max_instances=12 at 14:05. Burst capacity is currently DISABLED for this pool (policy=conservative).
kevin: If burst is off, can we toggle to allow ephemeral burst while we triage? Prefer gated enable + 5m rollback if errors persist.
sara: Running quick query for top 10 customers by rps in last 5m to identify noisy tenants. Command: ```redwoodctl metrics query --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --top-customers 10 --window 5m``` Will paste output in a sec.
ops-bot: Deploy check: no active deploys against models serving on this pool in last 30m.
sara: Output snippet: ```acme-corp: 420 rps
starter-app: 120 rps
internal-loadtest: 380 rps
unknown-xyz: 12 rps``` Looks like acme-corp + internal-loadtest are majority.
michael: Two mitigation paths: 1) enable burst capacity for pool + loosen kernel sched to reduce P95 (fast), 2) apply customer rate caps to top noisy tenants (safer, targeted). Recommend do both: enable burst and throttle internal-loadtest only.
lina: I can flip burst. Command I'll run: ```redwoodctl pools set-burst --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --enable --duration 10m --reason "emergent autoscale gating"``` Anyone object?
kevin: Go ahead on burst, but gate traffic: add a temporary routing rule to move lower-priority traffic to fallback model-variant to reduce token generation load.
sara: Applying rate limit for internal-loadtest, and a soft quota reduction for acme-corp to 300 rps with a 2-min cooldown: ```redwoodctl customers throttle --id internal-loadtest --rps 150 && redwoodctl customers quota --id acme-corp --rps 300 --temp 10m``` Will update support ticket after.
customer-success: Notifying account team for acme-corp and flagging support ticket #INC-4711. We'll prepare an incident message if impact persists.
lina: Burst enable in progress... ```API> pools/42/burst/enable => 202 Accepted``` Kernel sched adjustments applied, KV cache warm retained.
michael: Observing metrics — p95 dropping from 820ms -> 420ms after burst enable and throttles. Error rate trending down.
ops-bot: Autoscale events: +2 ephemeral burst instances provisioned at 14:10, will expire at 14:20 unless extended.
kevin: Good. Hold burst for 10m, monitor. If stable at 14:18 we keep and then gradually rollback throttles. Keep an eye on queue depth for long tail.
sara: I'll open a short-lived feature flag to divert non-critical routes to low-cost variant: ```feature-toggle set route/safe-fallback enabled --scope pool:eu-west-1```
customer-success: ACME is aware. They're not seeing user-facing errors yet, but monitoring. Keeping them in the loop.
michael: Partial handoff in 10m to next oncall. If anything regresses, re-escalate to infra lead @kevin. I'll stay until handoff completed.
next-oncall: Taking over at 14:20 UTC, will monitor next 30m. Ping me in-channel for any changes. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated (degraded) — burst enabled, per-customer throttles applied, fallbacks active. Next update due 14:25 UTC.
ops-bot: Note: created rollback plan and runbook reference -> https://console.redwood/internal/runbooks/dedicated-burst (runbook id RB-92)
michael: Logging timeline and summary to #postmortems draft. Please paste any commands you ran so we capture steps.
sara: Pasted commands into the support ticket and runbook. Will follow up with metrics dashboard link.
customer-success: Ticket updated. No escalation from ACME. Marking as monitored.
kevin: Re-evaluating scaling policy post-incident: propose raising max_instances for this pool and updating autoscale policy to allow short bursts automatically for tenants with reserved capacity. Will open RFC.
oncall-bot: Thread closed for active intervention; continue monitoring. If errors >2% within next 15m a new page will be triggered.
